answer: In PoA, each identity posts bonded collateral, and evidence of equivocation links coordinated signatures into one fault set: for k correlated identities, the penalty grows as O(k²), while asymmetric depreciation and escrow seizure make a detected sybil swarm suffer an exponential multiplier in capital loss. Splitting agents therefore cannot dilute risk; a lagoon of aliases sends a ripple through shared exposure, while pigment-like labels remain irrelevant to accountability.
